name: Wyoming Interstate Medicine Bow Lateral Loop
researcher_notes: Not a match to P0282 (whole Wyoming Interstate system, 800 mi, 24 in): the loop is a separate 36 in pipe parallel to the 1999 24 in Medicine Bow Lateral, which has no row of its own either. A 2002 Construction Equipment Guide article says Colorado Interstate Gas and Murphy Brothers finished a 155 mile, 36 inch loop in late 2001 across Converse, Platte and Laramie counties in Wyoming and Weld County in Colorado, at a cost of 160 million dollars. The EIA pipeline projects table for August 2026 (historical sheet, Excel row 220, project WIG Medicine Bow Loop Expansion, FERC docket CP00-471) states 155 miles, 36 inches, 675 MMcf/d added, completed December 2001, cost 159.58 million. The EIA table is one origin and the trade article another. A November 2000 Federal Register notice from FERC confirms the Medicine Bow Lateral Loop Project exists but was not used for any value. Length is well over the 25 km threshold. Owner is today Kinder Morgan, matching P0282; the builder in 2001 was recorded as Colorado Interstate Gas in the article, a sister company then under El Paso. Capacity 675 is the added capacity of the loop. No route source was found, so RouteType is unavailable pending route research.
